spec.description:
The ProctorWrap PlastiGrip is a 45mm diameter polypropylene
washer designed for the mechanical attachment of building wraps and rigid
insulation boards to timber and steel framing. Engineered with a flat base,
flexible perimeter, and a 5mm deep cupped head, it distributes clamping force
over a wide area to eliminate tear-out and wind blow-offs compared to
traditional staples. Tested in conjunction with ProctorWrap and ProctorPassive
membranes for calculating fixing span tables, it provides a weather-tight,
airtight mechanical anchor for high-wind building envelopes.
features: 45mm wide diameter distributes clamping force to prevent membrane tearing

5mm deep cupped head seals the washer to the substrate and protects fastener
heads

Flexible outer perimeter reduces risk of abrasion damage to building
wraps
Flat base design ensures flush mounting under claddings and battens

Superior alternative to staples, greatly reducing wind blow-off and pull-out
risk

Compatible with countersunk screws (8g-10g) for steel frames and
flat-head clouts for timber

Tested with ProctorWrap CW, HTS, and
ProctorPassive RS-IT for fixing span tables

Allows fastener spacing to be
increased to 600mm horizontal by 750mm vertical (4 per m²)

Manufactured from
durable, non-corrosive polypropylene material

AS/NZS 4200.2:2017

install:
Position
building wrap or rigid insulation board flat against timber or steel wall
framing

Insert 8g-10g countersunk screw (for steel) or flat-head clout nail
(for timber) through the PlastiGrip washer center

Fasten through the membrane
into the structural stud at recommended 600mm horizontal by 750mm vertical
spacing

Tighten screws only sufficiently to apply clamping force around the
perimeter of the washer

Do not over-tighten to avoid distorting the washer,
membrane, or substrate

If a washer is damaged or cracked as a result of
over-tightening, replace it prior to project completion

Use
corrosion-resistant screws or galvanised nails
selection_checklist:
Confirm framing substrate (timber studs require flat-head clouts; steel studs
require 8g-10g screws)

Calculate quantity needed based on approx. 4 washers
per square meter of wall wrap

Verify need for tear-resistant fixing in
high-wind regions or exposed sites

Ensure suitable corrosion-resistant screws
or nails are supplied by the builder
limitations:
Do not
over-tighten fasteners; excessive torque can crack the washer or distort the
substrate

Not recommended for permanent exposure to direct sunlight after
installation

Cladding must be installed within the UV exposure window of the
underlying membrane
